nodes.notes: Starts the workflow on a timer — every 6 h. No input data; downstream nodes fetch what they need.

nodes.name: Fetch Target Page
nodes.notes: GET https://example-market.com/posts — retries 3× with backoff on failure. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. nodes.name: Extract Listings (CSS)

nodes.name: Rows from Arrays

nodes.name: Load Previous Snapshot
nodes.notes: Reads every row from 'Post Tracker' — the read side of the store, e.g. for a digest or a downstream sync. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

nodes.name: Diff vs Last Run
nodes.notes: Diffs two streams by key into 4 lanes: only-in-A, same, different, only-in-B — the heart of the sync.

nodes.name: Alert New Findings
nodes.notes: Sends an email via Microsoft Outlook — recipient comes from the item's email field. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Microsoft OAuth2. Azure Portal → App registrations → Microsoft Graph → Mail.Send / Mail.Read.

nodes.name: Update Changed Rows
nodes.notes: Upserts a row into 'Post Tracker', matched on postId — re-running with the same key updates the row instead of duplicating it. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Google OAuth2 / service account. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

nodes.name: Write Fresh Snapshot
nodes.notes: Appends a new row to 'Post Tracker' — a human-readable audit trail that doesn't require opening n8n to inspect. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. nodes.name: Merge Diff Outcomes
nodes.notes: Rejoins 3 branches into one stream (mode: append) so downstream logic runs once. Watch out: Waits for every configured input. If one branch never produces items, add 'Always Output Data' upstream so this doesn't stall.

nodes.notes: Delegates to a reusable sub-workflow (single-responsibility building block) and waits for its result. Watch out: The sub-workflow needs an Execute Sub-workflow Trigger as its entry point. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run.

nodes.notes: Shapes the item: writes enrichedAt, enrichmentSource. Keeps the schema explicit between stages.

nodes.name: Stamp Completion Time
nodes.notes: Stamps completedAt with the current time for auditing.

nodes.name: Persist Run Metadata
nodes.notes: Saves key fields onto the execution record — searchable later in n8n's execution list.

nodes.name: Serialize Run Output (CSV)

nodes.name: Fingerprint for Idempotency
nodes.notes: Custom JavaScript: Build a stable idempotency key per post (djb2 hash, no deps) Watch out: Must return an array of items shaped like [{ json: {...} }].

nodes.name: Drop Already-Processed Items
nodes.notes: Cross-execution dedupe: remembers keys it has processed before and drops repeats — the idempotency guard. Watch out: Cross-execution memory persists. After changing the key field, clear stored keys or old keys keep matching.

nodes.notes: Saves key fields onto the execution record — searchable later in n8n's execution list.

nodes.name: Guard Non-Empty content
nodes.notes: Drops items that fail the condition; only qualifying items continue (no false branch).

# Track mentions of keywords: Google Sheets & Outlook

**Pattern:** Social Listening · **Level:** Expert · **Trigger:** Scheduled

## Overview

Runs on a schedule, and covers scheduling work end to end across Google Sheets, Outlook and Notion.

It moves through 28 working steps plus a 3-node error rail, in this order:

1. Hourly Schedule
2. Fetch Target Page
3. Extract Listings (CSS)
4. Rows from Arrays
5. Load Previous Snapshot
6. Diff vs Last Run
7. Alert New Findings
8. Update Changed Rows
9. Write Fresh Snapshot
10. Merge Diff Outcomes
11. Offload to Post-Process Sub-workflow
12. Record Sub-workflow Result
13. Load Previous Snapshot 2
14. Compute Drift vs Snapshot
15. Enrich with Reference Data
16. Fold In Enrichment Fields
17. Stamp Completion Time
18. Persist Run Metadata
19. Serialize Run Output (CSV)
20. Archive Row Snapshot
21. Fingerprint for Idempotency
22. Drop Already-Processed Items
23. Save Execution Metadata
24. Guard Non-Empty content
25. Stamp Processing Time
26. Summarize Run Stats
27. Append Audit Row (Google Sheets)
28. Send Summary to Outlook

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Outlook → Park in Dead-Letter Queue — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing scheduling work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

Hourly Schedule → Fetch Target Page → Extract Listings (CSS) → Rows from Arrays → Load Previous Snapshot → Diff vs Last Run → Alert New Findings → Update Changed Rows → Write Fresh Snapshot → Merge Diff Outcomes → Offload to Post-Process Sub-workflow → Record Sub-workflow Result → Load Previous Snapshot 2 → Compute Drift vs Snapshot → Enrich with Reference Data → Fold In Enrichment Fields → Stamp Completion Time → Persist Run Metadata → Serialize Run Output (CSV) → Archive Row Snapshot → Fingerprint for Idempotency → Drop Already-Processed Items → Save Execution Metadata → Guard Non-Empty content → Stamp Processing Time → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (Google Sheets) → Send Summary to Outlook → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Outlook → Park in Dead-Letter Queue

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Google Sheets and Outlook aligned by hand for scheduling
- Reconciling Google Sheets against Outlook after the two quietly drifted apart
- Scheduling work where "Fetch Target Page" is still a manual step before Google Sheets
- Scheduling work that only reaches Google Sheets on a schedule, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps Google Sheets and Outlook in step for scheduling, without anyone re-typing a row
- Compares Google Sheets against Outlook before writing, so only genuine differences land
- Safe to re-run: records already in Google Sheets or Outlook are skipped, across all 31 nodes of this scheduling build
- A failed Google Sheets or Outlook call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 31 nodes in this scheduling build
- Branches rejoin before Google Sheets, so a scheduling run reports once rather than 31 times

## Before first run
Connect credentials: API key / bearer for the target API; Google OAuth2 / service account; Microsoft OAuth2; Notion integration token.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

Every run diffs against the previous snapshot instead of re-alerting on everything scraped — without this, the workflow would spam the same unchanged listings on every scheduled run. The three-way split (new / changed / unchanged) means each gets exactly the treatment it needs: alert, update, or a silent snapshot refresh.

## Practice exercises

About as deep as this pattern goes — extend it:

1. Change the CSS selectors to scrape a different site's listing structure.
2. Manually edit one row in the snapshot store and confirm it's flagged as changed on the next run.
3. Add a price-drop-specific alert condition on top of the generic new/changed diff.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**API key / bearer for the target API**
Whatever the target API issues — usually a bearer token or API key.
_Gotcha:_ Store it as a credential, never typed into the node's parameters.

**Google OAuth2 / service account**
Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Using a Service Account? Share the spreadsheet with its email address or it 404s.

**Microsoft OAuth2**
Azure Portal → App registrations → Microsoft Graph → Mail.Send / Mail.Read.
_Gotcha:_ Choose delegated vs application permissions deliberately; they behave differently.

**Notion integration token**
notion.so/my-integrations → New integration → copy the Internal Integration Token.
_Gotcha:_ Then open the database → ••• → Connections → add your integration, or every call 404s.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**HTTP node returns 401 or 403**
Cause: Wrong or unscoped credential, or the API expects a header this request isn't sending.
Fix: Verify the key directly with curl first, then confirm the auth type matches what the API documents.

**HTTP node returns 429**
Cause: Rate limited by the provider.
Fix: Raise the wait between calls or lower the batch size. Retries already back off, but they cannot beat a hard quota.

**Execution stalls at the Merge node**
Cause: One input branch produced no items, so Merge is still waiting.
Fix: Enable 'Always Output Data' on the node feeding the empty branch.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Failures are also parked in a dead-letter queue for replay. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🧹 Data quality

Dedupe/diff steps make re-runs safe: the same input twice will not create duplicate records. If you change the key fields, clear n8n's dedupe memory (node → 'Clear stored keys') before the next run.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your scheduling process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Google Sheets: share the single spreadsheet with the service account rather than granting drive-wide access.
- Outlook: use `Mail.Send` alone if nothing here reads the mailbox.
- Notion: share only the target database with the integration. An integration sees nothing you have not explicitly shared.

The HTTP node sends a secret: keep it in a header credential, never in the URL — query strings land in proxy and execution logs.

**Do not log**
Log the identifier and the outcome, not the whole scheduling payload. n8n stores execution data verbatim, so anything a node emits is readable by everyone with instance access.
